name: Modularization-of-Thought (MoT) for Code Generation
executive_summary: Decompose a code-generation task into modular sub-problems before writing any code, mirroring how a human engineer would break a large function into smaller helper functions.
description: Applies decomposition-style reasoning (in the spirit of Least-to-Most Prompting) specifically to code: identify natural module/function boundaries in the target program before generating any implementation, then generate each module with awareness of the others' interfaces.
when_to_use: Code-generation tasks large or complex enough to naturally decompose into multiple functions/modules.
when_not_to_use: Small, single-function code-generation tasks where decomposition is pure overhead.
known_pitfalls: Interface mismatches between independently-generated modules are a real failure mode if module boundaries/signatures aren't fixed before generation.
